data.narrative:
Claros is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Daniel Kultran and Grant Verstandig that has raised $30M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises nine private peers alongside one public comparable (LNZA), including later-stage companies such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, as the peer-median approach cannot be applied due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables. The stage-progression method uses the $30M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage transitions, implying a valuation of $75M. This methodology is grounded in observed pricing dynamics at the seed-to-Series A inflection but carries inherent sensitivity to the multiplier assumption and to the representativeness of the $30M raised figure as a valuation proxy.

The triangulation yields a median valuation of $75M, with a low bound of $64M and high bound of $86M reflecting ±15% sensitivity around the central case. The narrow methodological foundation—relying on a single applicable approach—represents the primary valuation uncertainty. Tightening this range would require either (i) identification of same-stage Climate & Energy peers with disclosed valuations, or (ii) refinement of stage-specific step-up multiples within the sector. Until then, the $75M median should be treated as indicative rather than definitive.
